:::{#exm-wlln-auto}
#### The average fuel economy of many randomly drawn cars settles near the population mean

Take the cars in the Auto data described in @exm-clt-auto as the whole population.
Let $X_i$ be the fuel economy (`mpg`) of the $i$th car
drawn [at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice), with replacement.
The draws are [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid).
By [the population-mean proposition](expectation.qmd#prp-population-mean-expectation),
their population mean $\mean$
is the [average](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-mean) `mpg` over all the cars.
The code for @fig-wlln-auto draws $10{,}000$ cars.
It then plots the running average $\samplemean{X}{n}$ of the first $n$ draws
against $n$.

```{r}
#| label: fig-wlln-auto
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Running average of the fuel economy of cars drawn at random,
#|   with replacement, from the Auto data.
#|   The dashed line is the population mean.
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A line plot with the number of draws on a logarithmic horizontal axis
#|   from 1 to 10,000 and the running average miles per gallon
#|   on the vertical axis. The line swings by several miles per gallon
#|   over the first few draws, then narrows and stays close to
#|   a dashed horizontal line at the population mean, about 23.4.
auto <- readr::read_csv("data/auto.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
mu <- mean(auto$mpg)

n_draws <- 10000
set.seed(571)
draws <- sample(auto$mpg, size = n_draws, replace = TRUE)
draw_number <- seq_len(n_draws)
running <- tibble::tibble(
  n = draw_number,
  running_mean = cumsum(draws) / n
)

running |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = n, y = running_mean) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = mu, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Number of draws n", y = "Running average mpg")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# The claims the prose makes: the running average is far from the mean
# early on and close to it after all the draws.
miss <- abs(running$running_mean - mu)
early <- miss[1:10]
late <- miss[1000:n_draws]
miss_early <- max(early)
miss_late <- max(late)
stopifnot(miss_late < 0.5, 5 * miss_late < miss_early)
```

The population mean is $\mean =$ `{r} sprintf("%.2f", mu)` miles per gallon.
Over the first $10$ draws,
the running average misses it by as much as
`{r} sprintf("%.2f", miss_early)` miles per gallon.
From draw $1{,}000$ on,
it never misses by more than
`{r} sprintf("%.2f", miss_late)`.

:::
